pairs.subject: subprocess-lifecycle
pairs.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/headless.rs:72 Closing or hibernating a fleet session kills only the root pid, with no polite rung, no deadline and no tree kill, so a closed claude session can orphan its MCP servers and tool shells; the earlier verdict still holds, with only line numbers moved.

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/headless.rs:72 PidKiller does a single-pid forcible kill through sysinfo. There is no graceful rung, no deadline, and no descendants are killed. No kill_tree, job object or taskkill /T appears anywhere in commands/fleet.

src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/registry.rs:554 kill_child_of is the one close/hibernate door and goes straight to the forcible kill. Its outcome vocabulary is Killed, Failed or NoChild and never records a rung.

src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/headless.rs:1308 The first non-UTF-8 line ends the whole stream-json event loop, as the code's own comment at line 1384 says. Later events are drained to sink and never parsed. The standard keeps valid lines and decodes each line on its own.

src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/headless.rs:771 Ordinary headless spawns inherit the whole host environment minus a denylist. Only door runs are env_clear()-built (line 786), so the minimal environment is not the default.
src-tauri/src/commands/fleet/stale.rs:79 Per-session silence degrades the session to stalled at 2 minutes, separately from the 6-minute stale cutoff, so stalled and slow are told apart.

pairs.evidence: src-tauri/engine/src/session_pool.rs:145 The warm-session fingerprint hashes how many tools there are, not which tools, and leaves out credentials and the CLI version, even though the module header promises credential invalidation; swapping one tool or credential resumes a session built under a different configuration.

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/engine/src/session_pool.rs:145 The fingerprint is prompt, structured prompt, model, tool count and capabilities. It has no tool identity, credential or binary version, which contradicts the header at line 9.
src-tauri/engine/src/session_pool.rs:9 The documented invalidation trigger is not realized by compute_config_hash. The take site (executions.rs:596) passes tools.len().
src-tauri/src/engine/resource_governor.rs:29 Admission is pressure-aware with separate pause and resume watermarks (hysteresis) for both CPU and RAM.
src-tauri/engine/src/queue.rs:194 There are layered caps, global plus per-persona max_concurrent, and overflow is queued by priority.
